neighbours.label: A verb that joins one thing to another (connect, link, attach, join), vs verbs that only place or move things near each other
fire: In the old house, a secret passage connects the library to the cellar.
Each wagon is attached to the one in front by a steel hook.
A long cable links the satellite dish to the receiver.
The plumber joined the two pipes with a brass fitting.
Our office network connects every printer to the same server.
The badge attaches to your jacket with a small magnet.
A ferry route links the two islands every hour.
Tendons connect the muscles of the leg to the bones.
quiet: In the old house, a narrow staircase leads down to the cellar.
Each wagon is painted red with a white stripe on the side.
A long cable lies on the floor behind the receiver.
The plumber cleaned the two pipes with a wire brush.
Our office network is slow every morning at nine.
The badge is printed with your name and photo.
A ferry sails between the two islands every hour.
Tendons can become sore after a long run in the hills.
